sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: AI for Beginners is a free 12-week, 24-lesson Microsoft curriculum on artificial intelligence. It covers symbolic AI, neural networks, computer vision, natural language processing, genetic algorithms, reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems and AI ethics, with Jupyter notebooks in PyTorch and TensorFlow.
sixtySeconds.problem: AI courses often jump straight to one framework or skip the foundations. This curriculum walks through the main approaches to AI with theory, runnable notebooks, labs and quizzes, at a beginner-friendly pace.
whoFor: Beginners learning AI and deep learning
Students and teachers wanting a structured curriculum
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a broad, free foundation in AI with code in two major frameworks. It doesn't cover classic machine learning (see ML for Beginners) or business AI.
requirements: PyTorch or TensorFlow, depending on the notebook
Or VS Code with a Codespace

overview: The curriculum has 24 lessons plus extras across seven parts: introduction and history of AI; symbolic AI with knowledge representation and expert systems; neural networks from perceptrons to building your own framework; computer vision (CNNs, transfer learning, autoencoders, GANs, object detection, segmentation); NLP (embeddings, RNNs, transformers, named entity recognition, large language models); other techniques (genetic algorithms, deep reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems); and AI ethics.

Each lesson has pre-reading, executable Jupyter notebooks (often in both PyTorch and TensorFlow), labs for some topics, and links to Microsoft Learn modules. Quizzes are in a quiz app that can run locally or online.

For complete beginners, an examples folder has short programs such as Hello AI World, a simple neural network, an image classifier and text sentiment. A setup lesson and a guide for running in VS Code or a Codespace help you get started. The repository includes 50+ translations, so a sparse clone is recommended.
